turns.t: Morning! Right, so my big toe blew up like a balloon overnight on Tuesday, and I couldn't even put a sheet over it.
That sounds miserable. Which toe, and how is it now?
Left big toe. It's calmer now, but still red, and when it was at its worst, the pain woke me at three in the morning.
Has it happened before?
Once, I think. Last year? Or the year before that. I honestly couldn't tell you when, I just remember it was a bank holiday.
Okay, I'll note that you can't date it. Have you had any fever, or felt unwell with it?
No fever. Felt fine otherwise.
Did you knock it or injure it?
No, nothing. I'd have remembered.
Any other joints swollen?
No, just the toe.
What did you take for it?
Naproxen, 250 mg, twice a day, maybe? I took a few from my wife's pack, then I took them when I remembered, so it was a bit random.
Understood. So 250 mg twice a day as you recall it, but taken when you remembered. Any health conditions?
High blood pressure, that's all.
What do you drink, and how's your diet?
Five or six pints at the weekend, and I do love a prawn curry. Well, I did.
Let me check your pulse and blood pressure, and then look at the toe. ~
Go on. ~
Pulse 80, blood pressure 138 over 88, temperature 36.8.
Good. ~
Now the toe, tell me if it hurts.
Ow. Yes, there. ~
The base of the big toe is a bit red and warm, and tender when I press. No swelling elsewhere in the foot.
Gout? Everyone says gout. ~
I'm not going to put a name on it from one look. It's a typical picture, but I'd rather confirm it. I'd like to arrange a blood test for uric acid.
When? ~
Ideally two weeks after an attack, when it's settled, so book it in a fortnight. ~
Right. And the tablets? ~
Don't take someone else's tablets, please. Rest the foot, raise it, and cool it with a cold pack wrapped in a cloth.
Fair. What about the beer? ~
Less beer and fewer prawns would help, and plenty of water.
Ah. I'll try. ~
